q: Which Meta campaigns are wasting money?

checks.what: tool: uses spend plus an outcome metric

answer:
Short answer: several Meta campaigns are spending meaningful budget while delivering well below break‑even (Net ROAS < 1.0 on order-date), so they are losing money. Biggest offenders last 7 complete days (2026-10-07 → 2026-10-13, order-date):

- TH-383-SUSPENDER-29SEP — Spend ₹24,101 · Net ROAS 0.56x
- TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ — Spend ₹23,525.58 · Net ROAS 0.48x
- TH-222-WINGBIRD-23SEP — Spend ₹21,626.14 · Net ROAS 0.70x
- TH-279-BATHEASEBRUSH-07OCT — Spend ₹10,111.10 · Net ROAS 0.15x
- TH-445-PROSUSPENDERBOOTS-6OCT — Spend ₹7,398.58 · Net ROAS 0.06x
- CAT TOY CS-26SEP — Spend ₹9,707.40 · Net ROAS 0.16x

What this means (by impact)
- These campaigns drove the largest Meta spend but produced net returns well below 1.0x (i.e., contribution margin ÷ ad spend < 1), so ad dollars exceed contribution margin — a direct loss on the P&L.
- The highest absolute waste is from the two TH-383 campaigns together: total Meta ad spend for those two campaigns in the period was ₹47,626.59.
- Several smaller‑spend campaigns (BatheaseBrush, ProSuspenderBoots, Cat Toy) have very low ROAS (0.06–0.16x) and should be paused or reviewed immediately because each rupee spent there yields almost no contribution margin.
- Confidence: numbers are order-date P&L basis (net ROAS) for Meta only; data refreshed hourly and covers 2026-10-07..2026-10-13.
